title: Make the stock-take report add up while transfers run

blocks.text: A chain of about thirty shops keeps one product in `StockLedger`: units per warehouse. Transfer threads move units between warehouses a few times a minute; nothing is ever added or sold here, so the chain's total never changes. The stock-take report prints one line per warehouse on a label printer, which takes about a second per line, and then the total.

Last month's reports printed lines that didn't add up to the total the chain holds, and the auditors flagged every one. Someone suggested locking the ledger while the report prints, but a transfer must not wait half a minute for the printer.

Finish `src/main/java/practice/StockLedger.java`: hold the stock however you need to (the `ConcurrentHashMap` is only where the team started), and write `move` and `report`. When you're done, every report's lines add up to a total the chain really held, even with transfers running during it, and a transfer never waits for the printer. About twelve lines in total.

cases.says: after some moves, a report lists every warehouse with its units and returns their total
a report printed while units move between warehouses still lines up with one total that the chain really held
a move from a transfer thread returns while a report is still printing

origin.section: A Total That Must Add Up Needs a Snapshot or a Lock, and Size Decides Which

concepts: A read that must agree across elements needs a snapshot published whole or a lock held by writers and the reader alike.
